source: STYLE – how things are drawn (the creator's chosen YouTube explainer, 2026-11-07): flat shapes and icons, text as grey bars, one orange focus. Judge how simple and clear the drawing is against this.
tiles: 1: two avatar circles in the middle, four flat icons around them (timer, palette, note, camera); two icons bright, two dimmed – nothing to read
2: the same two avatars; the icons have flown into ONE card under them with an orange folder – the idea 'everything in one place' shown by grouping
3: a pipeline: an orange mascot, the card with the icons, three empty cards joined by one thin line – text is grey bars, not words
4: two app windows side by side: the left one alive (preview, timeline, one orange pause button), the right one blurred under a lock with ONE number '48,193 waiting' and one button
5: one label 'huashu-motion' with a GitHub icon over four video cards drawn as simple grey shapes
takeaways: Almost no words: text is drawn as grey rounded bars; the only real words are the one thing that matters (a name, a number, a button).
Few big flat shapes and icons (2–6 per frame), a lot of empty dark space around them.
ONE accent colour (orange) marks where to look; everything else is grey, dimmed or blurred.
The story is told by what the shapes do – gathering into a card, lining up into a chain, one window locked – not by labels.
No code, no logs, no file names, no small UI details anyone would try to read.

source: STYLE depth – how things are drawn in this style (the creator's chosen videos, 2026-11-08): real logos and real website screenshots in glass cards, a coloured glow per scene, some light scenes, a giant faint motif behind, a persistent dock.
tiles: 1: a big glass app-icon square with a huge '5', behind it tilted cards with REAL tool logos and blurred real website screenshots; a dock of 5 real tool icons under it; navy with a blue glow

2: a two-line headline (white, then grey), a glass Claude Code window with the prompt and 5 tool chips and a blue progress bar; under it a timeline strip of real thumbnails with a playhead and a waveform
3: three phones/tablets fanned out showing REAL websites; the middle one lists three words, the active one a solid blue pill; a waveform with a playhead below

4: LIGHT scene – off-white background with huge faint HTML code behind; a browser card 'github.com/…' with the real logo on a white header, the name and a '★ 55k' pill; the dock with the active tool glowing
5: LIGHT scene – a giant faint GitHub octocat silhouette, a teal glow, a huge number with a short line under it, stars and a rising line chart
6: dark blue – faint code and a giant faint '2' behind; a browser card with the real Remotion logo on white, its name and a star pill; the dock, the active icon ringed in blue
7: a blue 'render 100%' pill, a glass card with an icon and two words, film strips of the real logo crossing diagonally with motion blur
8: vivid – the frame filled with a grid of real purple template cards, a magnifier lens enlarging one of them; dark headline on top
9: purple glow – a huge '24' with the command names as a faint word cloud; a glass list of 3 commands, the first one lit; a blurred big example card below
10: LIGHT scene – a real ocean video in a player card, an audio pill with a waveform and a pause button, a '1 000+' pill, a strip of real photo thumbnails
11: amber glow – the real logo and the name, a browser card with the real site, a 'free' pill, a row of colour swatches
12: a real video frame in a card, a button with a click ripple and a cursor, a row of thumbnails with the chosen one ringed in amber
13: a big two-line headline, a browser card with the real site (mixkit.co) and its logo row, a teal/purple glow below
takeaways: Real things everywhere: real logos, real website screenshots in browser cards with the URL in a pill, real photos and video thumbnails – almost nothing is a drawn mock-up.
One glass focal card per frame with a coloured glow behind it; the colour changes per scene (blue, teal, purple, amber), and about one scene in four is LIGHT (off-white).
A giant faint motif behind the card that belongs to the topic: code, a huge number, a logo silhouette, a grid of the product's cards, blurred side cards.
Headline at the top in one or two lines (white, second line grey), clean bold sans; numbers are huge.
Small supporting pieces that move: a dock of the video's tools, a star pill, a waveform with a playhead, a timeline strip, a cursor clicking.

source: COMPOSITION – how a vertical frame is laid out (InsiderForce, TikTok, 10 frames, docs/bd/kadrai/insiderforce/): one dominant thing, big words, calm space. Judge the layout of the frame against this.
tiles: 1: three tool logos on a thin line at the top, ONE big pricing card in the middle – a single dominant thing
2: two logos, a video frame, then the headline in three sizes with the key phrase in a black box
3: price cards stacked in one repeated form; only the new price is in the accent colour
4: a globe joined by one line to a big character – one object fills the frame, the caption below with the key word bigger and bold
5: four logos in a diamond, dashed lines to one globe with a warning sign – a whole problem as one small, airy diagram
6: a character top left, one dashed curve to a logo bottom right, the words between them
7: a badge "01" on a line down to one screenshot card – the step and its result joined
8: a big character with a gear and three short rows with icons – few rows, very big
9: one character filling the frame, a two-line caption under it
10: a small strip of photos at the top, three short rows with ✦, the closing phrase bold
takeaways: One thing dominates every frame; everything else is clearly smaller or a thin line.
Words are big: the caption is 2–3 lines with the key words bold or boxed – never small labels to read.
A diagram has at most four nodes, lots of space between them, and one link drawn at a time.
Lots of calm space; nothing touches the edges or the caption.
The background colour is theirs (light) – judge the composition, not the colours.

source: Explainer frames from several creators, docs/bd/kadrai/geri/ (mechanism, setup, item, problem)
tiles: 1: a level title on top, ONE vertical diagram in the middle: three boxes, input → model → output, thin dashed arrows
2: the same title, the diagram replaced by two big rows with ✗ – what it cannot do
3: a simple drawing (an island with gorillas) with two tiny labels where it changed – the idea as one picture
4: one coloured ring of letters, the name big below – a whole concept as one shape
5: spotlight: one node bright, everything else dark and blurred, the key words in bold yellow below
6: a word on top, a drawing with ONE curved arrow showing what moves
7: the step number, the feature as a big pill, the tool's window under it
8: a counter in the corner, one animated map filling the frame, the caption at the bottom
9: a huge STEP and number in opposite corners, framing the speaker
10: a few words above one broken object (a cracked 'Tokens' plate) – the problem as one thing
takeaways: A diagram has 3–4 boxes in ONE direction with lots of space – never two diagrams in one frame.
When the explanation moves on, the picture is REPLACED (diagram → two ✗ rows) instead of squeezing a second one in.
One shape carries the concept (a ring, an island, a broken plate); labels are few and big.
Spotlight: to point at one part, everything else is dimmed.

source: Hooks, reveals, proof and CTA frames from several creators, docs/bd/kadrai/geri/
tiles: 1: the result on top, the claim in two big lines, the tools' logos in a zigzag below
2: text only – lines in different sizes, the brand set as one of the lines in its colours
3: two names stacked, one icon overlapping the other, the time promise below
4: a short line over one tool card, decorations only in the corners
5: three lines in three weights, the last in a black box
6: the browser cropped bottom right, the address big and readable
7: before/after as two equal cards stacked, a one-word label on each
8: a phone on the left, ONE benefit word on the right
9: one sentence in the middle, the key words in the accent colour
10: the comment keyword the biggest thing, the gift (an e-book) as an object
takeaways: The hook's first frame says the promise in 2–3 big lines with one word boxed or coloured.
Two equal things are right only for a before/after – then they get one word each.
A CTA makes the one keyword the biggest thing on screen.
Text-only frames are fine when the type itself has hierarchy: sizes, weights, one box.

source: InsiderForce frames that carry a real picture, docs/bd/kadrai/geri/picture-01..04
tiles: 1: a metaphor as a cut-out picture – a robot hand holding a glowing globe fills the top half; the claim below in big type, the last word boxed
2: a cut-out object (a blue folder labelled API's) with two hands reaching to it (Michelangelo) – the thing and the promise around it
3: a cut-out photo of the real person, black and white, over an accent shape; the headline beside him
4: four photo cards, tilted with shadows, in the corners around one number in a ring – real examples around the key fact
takeaways: One or two real pictures make a video feel alive: a metaphor, the real thing, the real person, real examples.
Pictures are cut out (no background) with a soft shadow, or set as tilted cards with a white border – never a flat rectangle pasted in.
The picture is big – it is the frame's main element, the words go above or beside it.
Black-and-white photos plus one accent colour keep a mixed set of pictures in one style.
